name: Vascular and vein care
summary: How expats find vascular surgeons and vein clinics in Singapore for varicose veins, DVT follow-up, peripheral artery disease, and dialysis access — clarifying medical vascular care versus cosmetic vein packaging.
body:
Vascular care covers arteries and veins: claudication, carotid disease, aneurysms, deep vein thrombosis (DVT) follow-up, venous ulcers, and varicose vein treatment. Expats often meet the specialty after a long-haul flight clot scare, non-healing leg wounds, or cosmetic concern about visible veins.

## Medical vs cosmetic framing
Varicose and spider veins sit on a spectrum. Symptoms (ache, swelling, skin changes, bleeding, ulcer risk) push toward duplex ultrasound and vascular assessment. Purely cosmetic thread veins may be handled in aesthetic-leaning vein clinics — still verify the proceduralist's credentials and facility standards. Insurance is far more likely to engage when there is documented reflux with symptoms than for appearance-only packages.

## DVT and travel
Post-flight leg swelling needs urgent GP/A&E triage when unilateral, painful, or associated with breathlessness (rule out PE). After diagnosis, anticoagulation follow-up and thrombophilia decisions may involve haematology and vascular input. Keep your long-haul itinerary and prior clot history handy.

## Arterial disease
Smoking history, diabetes, and exertional leg pain deserve ankle-brachial index / imaging pathways, not only vein laser ads. Vascular surgery departments in public hospitals handle complex arterial reconstruction; private consultants can accelerate duplex and angiogram planning when time-sensitive.

## How to choose
Look for vascular surgeons or accredited vein centres that start with duplex ultrasound, explain CEAP staging in plain language, and quote thermal ablation / sclerotherapy options without forcing a same-day package. Ask about compression stocking protocols and return-to-flight advice after procedures.

## Practical tip
If you stand all day in humid weather, graduated compression and weight/leg-elevation basics still matter between procedures. Bring prior duplex reports — repeating every scan at each new clinic wastes cash and delays treatment.
whenToEngage: Symptomatic varicose veins or skin changes on the legs
Post-DVT venous follow-up after travel clot scare
Leg ulcers or claudication need vascular assessment
Quoted cosmetic vein package before duplex ultrasound
